AI NEWS DAILY — 16 Nov 2026

TOP STORY
Nvidia's board removed Jensen Huang as CEO, naming CFO Colette Kress interim five days before quarterly results. A petition to reinstate him passed 115,000 signatures, including nearly 6,000 current employees. Over $500B of preliminary AI infrastructure financing now sits under a leadership question, and earnings land into it this week.

5 KEY UPDATES
1. Meituan released LongCat-2.5 under the MIT licence: 1.6T parameters, ~48B active, trained entirely on Chinese accelerators. It scores 88.4 on Terminal Bench v2.1 against Claude Opus 5's 89.1.
2. Anthropic's IPO book is reported 6x oversubscribed at $70-78 a share, listing on Nasdaq as ANT on 19 Nov, targeting $1.3-1.4T — below earlier hopes.
3. Four nonprofits asked a San Francisco court to freeze frontier development at OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and SpaceX's AI division. No injunction is in force yet.
4. A federal judge let a DRAM supply-conspiracy suit against Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron proceed, treating the industry's pivot to HBM as evidence rather than excuse.
5. Edge0 published a 145B model that runs on one RTX 5090 at 98 tokens/sec — serious local coding agents on a desktop card, though the licence blocks commercial use.

CONCEPT OF THE DAY — The Harness Is the Product
Model capability is converging; what separates working agents is the loop around the weights — memory, sandboxes, reviewers, evaluation. Singularity-Bench found one model in one harness matching human engineers on all six end-to-end AI dev tasks while others averaged half, and found the eval framework itself hackable. AgentSSL showed agents find good pipelines but cannot pick which to deploy, losing up to 47 points. Harness choice, not model choice, is the durable decision.

Full briefing: https://dilip457.github.io/ai-news-daily/
